finding.claim: deleteAccount discards the return value of canDelete, so any authenticated user can delete any account by id (broken authorization / IDOR).
finding.source: AccountService.java:20 — caller-supplied `id` and `User u` on DELETE /accounts/{id}

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-controlled id
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads the target account
canDelete(u, a) called but boolean result discarded; no throw or return

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) is correct but its result is unused at :22. No assertCanDelete or other check between :20 and :23. Sibling closeAccount (:27-31) correctly uses assertCanDelete at :29, which confirms the omission is a bug.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) is a bool-returning check, but its result is discarded as a bare statement at :22. No assertCanDelete or other check sits between :20 and :23, and no other caller or wrapper exists in the repo (grep finds only the definitions and the closeAccount call at :29). The only control that works is assertCanDelete (:13-17), which closeAccount uses at :29 and deleteAccount does not.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement, so its false result never blocks accounts.remove(id) at :23, while the sibling closeAccount at :29 enforces assertCanDelete. A non-admin authenticated user can therefore delete another user's account by id. The HTTP route binding for DELETE /accounts/{id} is not in this repo, so reachability rests on the comment at :19.
